conceptCapsule.title: Mathematical & Physical Interpretation of Position-Time ($x$-$t$) Curves
conceptCapsule.summary: The instantaneous velocity is the first derivative / slope of the tangent to the $x$-$t$ graph ($v = \frac{dx}{dt} = \tan\theta$). The acceleration is determined by the curvature / concavity (second derivative): an upward-opening curve ($\frac{d^2x}{dt^2} > 0$) implies positive acceleration, while a downward-opening curve ($\frac{d^2x}{dt^2} < 0$) implies negative acceleration.
conceptCapsule.keyFormula: $$v = \frac{dx}{dt} = \text{Slope of } x\text{-}t \text{ graph}, \quad a = \frac{d^2x}{dt^2} = \text{Concavity of } x\text{-}t \text{ graph}$$
conceptCapsule.examTrap: The area under an $x$-$t$ graph has NO physical significance (units $\text{m}\cdot\text{s}$). Also remember that a single vertical line on an $x$-$t$ graph represents infinite velocity and simultaneous existence at multiple points, which is physically impossible. Direction reversal occurs when the slope crosses zero ($\frac{dx}{dt} = 0$).

questions.statement: In an $x$-$t$ graph, the slope of the tangent at any given instant represents:
questions.solution:
By definition of differential calculus in kinematics: $$\text{Slope} = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{\Delta x}{\Delta t} = \frac{dx}{dt} = v_{\text{inst}}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: An $x$-$t$ graph for a particle moving along a straight line is a parabola opening upwards ($x = kt^2$, $k > 0$). This motion corresponds to:

options.text: Non-uniformly accelerated motion with increasing acceleration

questions.solution:
1. For $x(t) = kt^2$, $v(t) = \frac{dx}{dt} = 2kt$.
2. Acceleration $a(t) = \frac{dv}{dt} = 2k = \text{constant} > 0$.
3. An upward opening parabola on an $x$-$t$ graph represents uniform positive acceleration.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: The $x$-$t$ graphs of two particles $A$ and $B$ are straight lines making angles of $30^\circ$ and $60^\circ$ with the time axis respectively. The ratio of their velocities $v_A / v_B$ is:
questions.solution:
1. $v_A = \tan(30^\circ) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$
2. $v_B = \tan(60^\circ) = \sqrt{3}$
3. Ratio: $$\frac{v_A}{v_B} = \frac{1/\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{1}{3}$$
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: If an $x$-$t$ curve is concave downwards ($\frac{d^2x}{dt^2} < 0$) in a given interval, the particle is experiencing:
questions.solution:
Curvature and concavity are dictated by the second derivative. Concave downward implies $\frac{d^2x}{dt^2} < 0$. Since acceleration $a = \frac{d^2x}{dt^2}$, it indicates negative acceleration.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: Which of the following position-time ($x$-$t$) graphs is physically IMPOSSIBLE?

options.text: An $x$-$t$ graph having a vertical tangent (infinite slope)
An $x$-$t$ graph with a horizontal tangent
An $x$-$t$ graph passing below the time axis

questions.solution:
A vertical tangent on an $x$-$t$ graph indicates $\frac{dx}{dt} \to \infty$, which would mean an infinite velocity. Furthermore, a vertical line implies that a body is present at multiple distinct positions simultaneously, which is unphysical.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: The $x$-$t$ graph of a particle is given by $x = 8t - 2t^2\text{ m}$. The particle reverses its direction of motion at time $t$ equal to:
questions.solution:
Direction reversal occurs when instantaneous velocity is zero: $$v(t) = \frac{dx}{dt} = 8 - 4t = 0 \implies 4t = 8 \implies t = 2\text{ s}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: If the $x$-$t$ graph of a moving particle is parallel to the time axis, the state of the particle is:
questions.solution:
A line parallel to the time axis means $x(t) = \text{constant}$, hence $v = \frac{dx}{dt} = 0$. The particle remains stationary at rest.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A particle moves along the $x$-axis. Its $x$-$t$ graph consists of two straight line segments: from $(0\text{ s}, 0\text{ m})$ to $(2\text{ s}, 10\text{ m})$ and from $(2\text{ s}, 10\text{ m})$ to $(5\text{ s}, 0\text{ m})$. The average velocity in the interval $t = 0$ to $5\text{ s}$ is:
questions.solution:
Net displacement $\Delta x = x(5) - x(0) = 0 - 0 = 0\text{ m}$.
$$v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{\Delta x}{\Delta t} = \frac{0\text{ m}}{5\text{ s}} = 0\text{ m/s}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: In the previous question, the average speed of the particle in the interval $t = 0$ to $5\text{ s}$ is:
questions.solution:
1. Distance from $0$ to $2\text{ s}$: $|10 - 0| = 10\text{ m}$
2. Distance from $2$ to $5\text{ s}$: $|0 - 10| = 10\text{ m}$
3. Total distance $= 20\text{ m} \implies \text{Average Speed} = \frac{20\text{ m}}{5\text{ s}} = 4\text{ m/s}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: The position of a particle is $x(t) = t^3 - 3t^2 + 2\text{ m}$. The inflection point on the $x$-$t$ curve (where acceleration is zero) occurs at:
questions.solution:
1. Velocity $v(t) = \frac{dx}{dt} = 3t^2 - 6t$
2. Acceleration $a(t) = \frac{dv}{dt} = 6t - 6$
3. Point of inflection occurs when $a(t) = 0 \implies 6t - 6 = 0 \implies t = 1\text{ s}$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A ball is thrown vertically upwards from the ground, reaches maximum height, and falls back to the thrower's hand. The correct $x$-$t$ graph (with upward direction taken as positive) is:

options.text: A straight line with positive slope
A straight line with negative slope

questions.solution:
The equation of vertical projectile motion is $y(t) = u t - \frac{1}{2}gt^2$. This is a quadratic equation with a negative second-degree coefficient ($-\frac{1}{2}g < 0$), representing a parabola opening downwards.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: Two particles $1$ and $2$ start from the same point. Their $x$-$t$ equations are $x_1 = 2t$ and $x_2 = 4t - t^2$. The time at which they meet again after $t = 0$ is:
questions.solution:
Meeting condition $x_1(t) = x_2(t)$:
$$2t = 4t - t^2 \implies t^2 - 2t = 0 \implies t(t - 2) = 0 \implies t = 2\text{ s}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: If the tangent to an $x$-$t$ curve makes an obtuse angle with the positive time axis, the instantaneous velocity is:
questions.solution:
Velocity is the slope $v = \tan\theta$. For an obtuse angle ($90^\circ < \theta < 180^\circ$), $\tan\theta < 0$, signifying that velocity is negative.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: In an $x$-$t$ graph, the area under the curve:
questions.solution:
The integral $\int x dt$ produces units of $\text{metre}\cdot\text{second}$, which does not correspond to any standard physical quantity in mechanics.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: For a particle executing simple harmonic motion $x = A\sin(\omega t)$, the slope of the $x$-$t$ graph is maximum at:
questions.solution:
Slope $v = \frac{dx}{dt} = A\omega \cos(\omega t)$. The magnitude is maximum ($|v| = A\omega$) when $\cos(\omega t) = \pm 1 \implies \sin(\omega t) = 0 \implies x = 0$ (the mean position).
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: The position-time graph of a body is shown as a complete circle of radius $R$. This graph is:

options.text: Physically unrealizable because time cannot flow backwards and one time cannot have two positions

questions.solution:
A circle in the $x$-$t$ plane violates two core physical tenets: (1) a single time instant would correspond to two different spatial positions, and (2) on the left half of the circle, time would be flowing backwards.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A car travels on a straight line. Its $x$-$t$ curve has $\frac{dx}{dt} > 0$ and $\frac{d^2x}{dt^2} > 0$ throughout. The car is:

options.text: Moving in positive direction with decreasing speed
Moving in positive direction with increasing speed (speeding up)
Moving in negative direction with increasing speed

questions.solution:
$\frac{dx}{dt} > 0 \implies$ velocity is positive (forward motion). $\frac{d^2x}{dt^2} > 0 \implies$ acceleration is positive. Since velocity and acceleration have the same sign, the particle is speeding up.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A particle moves according to $x(t) = 5\sin(2\pi t)\text{ m}$. In one full period $T = 1\text{ s}$, the number of times the slope of the $x$-$t$ graph becomes zero is:
questions.solution:
1. Slope is velocity: $v(t) = 10\pi \cos(2\pi t)$
2. In interval $0 \le t < 1\text{ s}$, $\cos(2\pi t) = 0 \implies 2\pi t = \frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{3\pi}{2} \implies t = 0.25\text{ s}$ and $t = 0.75\text{ s}$ (exactly 2 times).
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: The $x$-$t$ graph of a particle is given by $x(t) = a - b e^{-k t}$, where $a, b,$ and $k$ are positive constants. As $t \to \infty$, the velocity of the particle approaches:
questions.solution:
Velocity $v(t) = \frac{dx}{dt} = b k e^{-kt}$. As $t \to \infty$, $e^{-kt} \to 0 \implies v \to 0$.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: An elevator descends from rest at the top floor to the ground floor. Its position $y(t)$ measured from the ground floor as a function of time is best described by:

options.text: An initial downward curved parabola, followed by a linear descent, and ending with an upward curved parabola to rest
A single continuous straight line with negative slope

questions.solution:
1. Acceleration phase: downward curved parabola ($y = H - \frac{1}{2}at^2$).
2. Constant speed descent: linear graph with negative slope.
3. Braking to rest: upward curving parabola where positive upward acceleration brings velocity back to zero at $y = 0$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.
